│
├── Definition
│   └── The total monetary value of final goods and services produced within the economic territory of a country during one year, calculated at base year prices, is called Real GDP.
│
├── Also Known As
│   └── Constant Price GDP
│
├── Important Features
│   ├── Uses base year prices
│   ├── Removes effect of inflation
│   ├── Shows actual production growth
│   └── Better measure of economic growth
│
├── Formula
│   └── Real GDP = Quantity × Base Year Price
│
├── Example
│   ├── 100 mobile phones produced
│   ├── Base year price = ₹15,000 per phone
│   └── Real GDP contribution = ₹15,00,000
│
├── Real GDP vs Nominal GDP
│   ├── Real GDP → Base year prices
│   └── Nominal GDP → Current prices
│
├── Details (Paragraph)
│   └── Real GDP refers to the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within the economic territory of a country during one year using base year prices. Since inflation is removed, Real GDP provides a more accurate measure of actual production and economic growth.
│
└── Quick Trick
    └── Real = Base Year Price | Nominal = Current Price

GDP Deflator (Inflation Measure)
│
├── Definition
│   └── GDP Deflator is a measure used to calculate inflation by comparing Nominal GDP with Real GDP.
│
├── Purpose
│   ├── Measures price changes in the economy
│   ├── Shows impact of inflation
│   └── Converts Nominal GDP into Real GDP
│
├── Formula
│   └── GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100
│
├── Important Features
│   ├── Measures overall price level changes
│   ├── Covers all final goods and services
│   ├── Changes with consumption pattern
│   └── Broader than CPI and WPI
│
├── Example
│   ├── Nominal GDP = ₹500 lakh
│   ├── Real GDP = ₹400 lakh
│   └── GDP Deflator = (500/400) × 100 = 125
│
├── Interpretation
│   ├── GDP Deflator = 100 → No inflation
│   ├── Above 100 → Inflation exists
│   └── Below 100 → Prices lower than base year
│
├── Difference
│   ├── CPI → Consumer goods only
│   ├── WPI → Wholesale prices
│   └── GDP Deflator → Entire economy
│
├── Details (Paragraph)
│   └── GDP Deflator is an important indicator used to measure inflation in an economy. It compares Nominal GDP with Real GDP to show how much of GDP growth is due to price rise rather than actual production increase. Since it includes all final goods and services produced in an economy, it is considered a broad measure of inflation.
│
└── Quick Trick
    └── Deflator = Price Change Detector

Gross National Product (GNP)
│
├── Definition
│   └── GNP is the total monetary value of final goods and services produced by the citizens of a country during one year, irrespective of whether production takes place inside or outside the country.
│
├── Important Features
│   ├── Based on nationality/citizenship
│   ├── Includes income earned abroad by citizens
│   ├── Excludes income earned by foreigners within country
│   └── Measures national production
│
├── Formula
│   └── GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)
│
├── Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)
│   ├── Income earned by citizens abroad
│   └── Minus income earned by foreigners domestically
│
├── Examples
│
│   ├── Included in GNP
│   │   ├── Income earned by Indian company in USA
│   │   ├── Salary earned by Indian working abroad
│   │   └── Production by Indian firms outside India
│   │
│   └── Not Included
│       ├── Income of foreign companies in India
│       └── Foreign workers' income inside country
│
├── GNP vs GDP
│   ├── GDP → Geography matters
│   └── GNP → Nationality matters
│
├── Example
│   ├── GDP = ₹100 lakh
│   ├── NFIA = ₹10 lakh
│   └── GNP = ₹110 lakh
│
├── Details (Paragraph)
│   └── Gross National Product (GNP) measures the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced by the citizens of a country during one year, regardless of whether production occurs inside or outside the country. It includes income earned abroad by citizens and excludes income earned domestically by foreigners. Therefore, GNP focuses on nationality rather than geographical boundaries.
│
└── Quick Trick
    └── GDP = Domestic Area | GNP = National People

Net Domestic Product (NDP)
│
├── Definition
│   └── NDP is the total monetary value of final goods and services produced within the economic territory of a country during one year after deducting depreciation from GDP.
│
├── Important Features
│   ├── Based on domestic/economic territory
│   ├── Depreciation is deducted
│   ├── Shows actual addition to economy
│   └── More accurate than GDP for measuring net production
│
├── Formula
│   └── NDP = GDP − Depreciation
│
├── Depreciation Meaning
│   ├── Wear and tear of machinery
│   ├── Loss in value of capital goods
│   └── Consumption of fixed capital
│
├── Examples
│   ├── GDP = ₹1000 crore
│   ├── Depreciation = ₹100 crore
│   └── NDP = ₹900 crore
│
├── NDP vs GDP
│   ├── GDP → Includes depreciation
│   └── NDP → Excludes depreciation
│
├── Details (Paragraph)
│   └── Net Domestic Product (NDP) refers to the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within the economic territory of a country during one year after subtracting depreciation from Gross Domestic Product (GDP). Since depreciation accounts for wear and tear of machines and capital goods, NDP gives a better picture of actual productive capacity.
│
└── Quick Trick
    └── Net = Minus Depreciation | Domestic = Inside Country

Net National Product (NNP)
│
├── Definition
│   └── NNP is the total monetary value of final goods and services produced by the citizens of a country during one year after deducting depreciation from GNP.
│
├── Important Features
│   ├── Based on nationality
│   ├── Depreciation is deducted
│   ├── Includes income earned abroad by citizens
│   └── Shows net national income generation
│
├── Formula
│   └── NNP = GNP − Depreciation
│
├── Depreciation Meaning
│   ├── Wear and tear of machinery
│   ├── Loss in value of capital goods
│   └── Consumption of fixed capital
│
├── Examples
│   ├── GNP = ₹1200 crore
│   ├── Depreciation = ₹200 crore
│   └── NNP = ₹1000 crore
│
├── NNP vs GNP
│   ├── GNP → Includes depreciation
│   └── NNP → Excludes depreciation
│
├── At Market Price & Factor Cost
│   ├── NNP at Market Price → Includes indirect taxes
│   └── NNP at Factor Cost → National Income
│
├── Details (Paragraph)
│   └── Net National Product (NNP) refers to the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced by the citizens of a country during one year after subtracting depreciation from Gross National Product (GNP). It reflects the actual net production of nationals and provides a more realistic measure of economic performance. NNP at Factor Cost is commonly called National Income.
│
└── Quick Trick
    └── National + Net = Citizens − Depreciation
